title: Runes and Soul Cores Reference
summary: Runes and Soul Cores are socketables placed into augment sockets on weapons and armour. This guide covers the difference, slot effects, tiers, and how to choose by build goal.
description: A source-linked reference for Runes and Soul Cores: Rune vs Soul Core, socket requirements, slot effect matrix, tiers, acquisition, and build goals.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Soul Core currency item icon - a burning soul essence container placed in augment sockets

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Runes and Soul Cores are socketables you insert into augment sockets on weapons and armour. Runes are common single-stat items; Soul Cores are rarer and stronger.
calloutDetail: The same Rune gives a different bonus depending on the slot it is placed in.
Sockets are added by Artificer's Orb on martial weapons and armour.

answers.label: Use a Rune
text: Use a Rune for a cheap, single-stat or resistance fix on the matching slot.

answers.label: Save a Soul Core
text: Save Soul Cores for your best base where the bigger bonus matters.

answers.label: Plan the slot
text: Match the socketable to the slot, not just the stat you want.

sections.title: Item family
intro: Runes and Soul Cores both occupy augment sockets, but they differ in rarity, strength, and how you should spend them.

members.title: Rune
body: A Rune grants one bonus that scales with its tier. Cheap and widely available, it is the default choice for filling a gap.

members.title: Soul Core
body: A Soul Core is rarer and usually grants a much larger or special effect. Reserve it for gear you will keep for a long time.

sections.title: Rune vs Soul Core
paragraphs: A Rune is the everyday socketable. It provides a single, predictable bonus and comes in Lesser, Normal, and Greater tiers so you can scale the effect with currency you can actually farm.

A Soul Core is the premium option. It is far less common and generally delivers a stronger or more specialized effect for the same slot. Because it is scarce, it is best saved for a base you intend to keep rather than a transitional item.
bullets: Soul Cores: rare, strong, often build-defining.

sections.title: Socket requirements
note: A socketable can only be inserted into an augment socket. Caster weapons cannot receive augment sockets, and corrupted or sanctified items have extra restrictions.

rows.label: Corrupted item
rows.note: Confirm current client behaviour before socketing.

sections.title: Slot effect matrix
note: The same socketable can produce a different bonus depending on the slot. Always check the in-game tooltip for the slot you plan to use.

sections.title: Acquisition
intro: Runes drop from general gameplay and can be farmed from specific content; Soul Cores are far rarer.

routes.label: World and map drops
body: Runes drop from monsters, chests, and strongboxes across the campaign and endgame.

routes.label: Vendor and currency exchange
body: Some tiers can be upgraded or acquired through vendor recipes and currency exchange where available.

routes.label: Soul Core sources
body: Soul Cores come from rarer content and high-value drops; expect to trade for them.

steps.label: Open the item
body: Right-click the item with an augment socket to open the socket view.

steps.label: Drag in the socketable
body: Place the Rune or Soul Core into the open socket.

steps.label: Confirm the slot bonus
body: Read the tooltip; the bonus depends on the slot.

sections.title: Replacement and extraction
paragraphs: You can replace a socketable by inserting a new one, but recovering the original usually requires Orb of Extraction or a similar recovery method.
Extraction has a cost and is not always available, so decide carefully before committing a Soul Core to a base you may replace.
bullets: Extraction cost varies; confirm before extracting.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Most builds use socketables to patch the one defensive or offensive hole the tree and gear cannot cover.

builds.title: Resistance cap
builds.description: Use a Rune on the slot that grants the resistance you are missing to hit 75%.

builds.title: Attribute fix
builds.description: A helmet or glove Rune can supply the attribute points needed to equip a key gem.

builds.title: Damage boost
builds.description: Weapon Runes and Soul Cores add the damage type your build scales.

sections.title: Choosing by stat goal
paragraphs: Decide the goal before opening the socket. A fire-resistance Rune belongs on the slot that grants resistance, not necessarily the weapon.
Prioritize: cap resistances first, then attributes for gem requirements, then defensive pool, then damage.
bullets: Missing fire/cold/lightning res -> resistance Rune on the resistance slot.
Short on Strength/Intelligence/Dexterity -> attribute Rune on helmet or gloves.
Already capped -> invest in life, armour, or damage.

entries.question: Why does my Rune give a different stat in another slot?
summary: A player expected the same bonus in every slot.
editorialAnalysis: Socketables scale with slot; the tooltip changes per slot.
officialAnswer: Check the tooltip for each slot before socketing.

entries.question: Can I get my Soul Core back?
summary: A player wanted to recover a committed Soul Core.
editorialAnalysis: Recovery needs Orb of Extraction and has a cost.
officialAnswer: Use extraction only when the base is being replaced.

directAnswer: The item needs an augment socket from Artificer's Orb first.
checks: Confirm the item is a martial weapon or armour with a free socket.

directAnswer: The slot changes the bonus; read the tooltip for that slot.
checks: Compare the weapon, chest, helmet, glove, and boot tooltips.

items.question: Is a Soul Core always better than a Rune?
answer: Usually stronger, but it is far rarer; use Runes for cheap fixes and save Soul Cores for lasting gear.

items.question: Can I move a socketable between items?
answer: You replace it by inserting a new one; recovering the old one needs extraction.

items.question: Why does the same Rune feel different per slot?
answer: The bonus scales with the slot; always read the per-slot tooltip.

changes: Runes and Soul Cores remain the socketable family for augment sockets on weapons and armour.
